name: Gemini App
description: Antigravity restyled after the Gemini app: the left sidebar, the model selector, the prompt box, and the conversation, with short model names on the prompt box pill and the agent's tools in the plus menu.
author: Yashjit Pal

patches.note: Cache the native color table until the root style/class, stylesheet count, or stylesheet content changes. Head mutations are filtered to styles and links: switching a conversation changes its title, which must not discard the color cache and force another style calculation. Stylesheet media, href, rel, and disabled changes still invalidate it.

patches.note: The hook behind the fading edges of every scrolling area watches the scroller and each of its children for resizes, and watches for rows being added or removed. Every one of those notifications measured the scroller immediately, so a chat list swapping rows in and out measured once per batch — the single most expensive thing in a profile of switching chats and collapsing the rail. Coalesce the notifications to one measurement per frame. The browser paints once per frame, so the fades land on exactly the same pixels; the first measurement after mount and the one driven by the scroll event are both left alone.

Every label in the sidebar that can be clipped runs a hook that measures whether it is clipped, on mount and on every resize, and writes the answer into React state. Measuring is a scrollWidth read, which has to be answered with the truth, so it forces the browser to lay the page out if anything has been written since the last time it did. One label per row, each measuring and then writing, means one full layout per row: the third most expensive thing in a profile of switching chats and collapsing the rail. Collect the measurements instead, then take all the readings together and write all the answers afterwards, so a rail full of rows costs one layout rather than one each. The reading itself is unchanged and still lands in the same task, before anything is painted.

Ref attachment, ResizeObserver registration, existing size caches, scrolling rules, and the measured values are unchanged. Jobs run in a microtask before paint; removed or reused rows are ignored. Other virtual lists keep the native path.

patches.note: Disable automatic following of growing responses and steps inside conversations while Gemini App is running. Preserve initial positioning, explicit jump-to-bottom, native user-scroll handling, and smooth/instant behavior. Remaining scroll requests are coalesced and all heights are read before any scrolling. The policy, batching helper, and explicit-jump callback are installed together by one guarded hook replacement; disabled Gemini App and unrelated viewports retain native following.

patches.note: Reuse the native artifact, upload, and command-palette projections when revisiting an unchanged artifact list. Each projection owns a separate cache with weak array keys and at most four recent lists. Entry identity, URI, timestamp object/fields, ordering, and workspace are checked before reuse. The original mapping, filtering, sorting, icons, error handling, and React hook order stay intact. Each complete component replacement includes its own cache so a version mismatch cannot leave an undefined helper.

patches.note: Opt the native markdown renderer into Gemini's streaming reveal while this plugin is running. One guarded replacement supplies the optional rehype/components hook, root ref, and React bridge; a host version mismatch cannot install half a hook. The ref lets the response footer wait for visual completion without observers or layout changes. The original renderer, markdown plugins, links, code, and wrapper layout are retained. The bridge falls back to the native renderer when Gemini App is disabled.
